articles.title: IFCE: 14 novos cursos técnicos e inscrições abertas no Ceará | G1
articles.standfirst: Novas formações serão ofertadas em oito cidades do Ceará, com opções de modalidades Integrado ao Ensino Médio e Subsequente.
articles.summary: Novas formações serão ofertadas em oito cidades cearenses, com opções de modalidades Integrado ao Ensino Médio e Subsequente.
articles.body:
O Instituto Federal do Ceará (IFCE) aprovou a criação de 14 cursos técnicos que serão ofertados em oito municípios . As novas formações são voltadas a áreas variadas, que incluem tecnologia da informação, negócios e serviços. Sete dos cursos já estão com processos seletivos abertos, e os outros sete devem ter editais lançados em breve.

Os cursos novos são em duas modalidades: Integrado ao Ensino Médio, para egressos do Ensino Fundamental; e Subsequentes, para egressos do Ensino Médio.

Segundo a instituição federal de ensino, as novas formações contribuem para a verticalização da oferta de ensino nos campi e se beneficiam da infraestrutura, do corpo docente e da experiência já existentes em cada unidade.

Veja abaixo a lista completa dos novos cursos:

Baturité : Técnico Subsequente em Panificação

Fortaleza : Técnico Integrado em Saneamento; Técnico Integrado em Tradução e Interpretação de Libras; Técnico Subsequente em Desenvolvimento Comunitário e Técnico Subsequente em Serviços de Restaurante Bar

Jaguaruana : Técnico Integrado em Programação para Jogos Digitais

Maranguape : Técnico Integrado em Eletrônica e Técnico Integrado em Inteligência Artificial

Mombaça: Técnico Integrado em Administração e Técnico Integrado em Informática

Paracuru : Técnico Integrado em Redes de Computadores

Tabuleiro do Norte : Técnico Integrado em Informática para Internet e Técnico Subsequente em Vendas

Ubajara : Técnico Integrado em Gastronomia

IFCE aprova 14 novos cursos técnicos em oito cidades — Foto: IFCE/Divulgação

Ainda conforme o IFCE, há outros 16 cursos técnicos em processo de criação. A expectativa da instituição é de que essas formações sejam finalizadas pela Pró-Reitoria de Ensino a tempo de lançarem os processos seletivos em 2027.

articles.title: Petrolina: cursos e oficinas gratuitas para jovens em outubro | G1
articles.standfirst: Atividades incluem oficinas, palestra, curso e ações sobre desenho, educação financeira, gastronomia, tecnologia e cidadania. Programação é voltada para pessoas de 15 a 29 anos.
articles.summary: Petrolina oferece cursos gratuitos e oficinas de desenho, educação financeira e design digital na Estação das Juventudes para pessoas de 15 a 29 anos em outubro.
articles.body:
Petrolina tem programação gratuita para jovens com oficinas, curso e palestra em outubro — Foto: Divulgação/Ascom PMP

A Estação das Juventudes, em Petrolina , no Sertão de Pernambuco, promove durante o mês de outubro uma programação gratuita voltada para jovens de 15 a 29 anos. A agenda reúne oficinas, palestra, curso e outras atividades relacionadas a criatividade, educação financeira, gastronomia, tecnologia e cidadania.

A programação começa nesta quinta-feira (8), das 14h às 17h, com a oficina “Desenhe o Seu Mundo: Oficina de Iniciação ao Desenho Artístico”. A atividade terá 20 vagas e propõe o uso do desenho como forma de observar, pensar e registrar o mundo ao redor.

No dia 15, das 14h às 17h, será realizada a palestra “O futuro que você quer viver começa nas escolhas que você faz hoje”, sobre educação financeira. A atividade abordará organização do dinheiro, escolhas de consumo e cuidados para evitar armadilhas financeiras.

Já no dia 20, das 8h às 12h, será realizada a oficina “Do Dendê ao Lucro”, que reúne o preparo do acarajé e noções de empreendedorismo e gestão de negócios.

A programação também inclui o Curso de Design Digital, iniciado em setembro e com aulas previstas até o dia 26 de outubro. A formação acontece de segunda a sexta-feira, das 8h às 12h, e apresenta ferramentas de design e Inteligência Artificial aplicadas à produção de materiais e ao dia a dia.

O curso oferece auxílio-transporte de R$ 250, lanche, material didático e certificado de conclusão de 100 horas. No dia 24, às 9h, a Estação das Juventudes participa de uma ação pelo Dia dos Professores, na Escola Antônio Padilha, com apoio à emissão da Identidade Jovem.

As atividades acontecem na Estação das Juventudes, localizada na BR-407, nº 571, Cohab Massangano, próxima ao Samu. As inscrições podem ser feitas presencialmente, de segunda a sexta-feira, das 8h às 17h, enquanto houver vagas.

Outras informações podem ser obtidas pelos telefones (87) 3983-6477 e WhatsApp (87) 99212-9449.

articles.title: É falsa foto de eleitores de vermelho com tornozeleira eletrônica | G1
articles.standfirst: Detector da OpenAI, dona do ChatGPT, aponta uso de ferramentas de inteligência artificial da empresa. Além disso, conteúdo tem distorções comuns a registros fabricados sinteticamente.
articles.summary: Foto tem distorções comuns em imagens produzidas com inteligência artificial; detector da OpenAI, dona do ChatGPT, aponta que conteúdo foi criado com ferramentas de IA da empresa.
articles.body:
É #FAKE foto de eleitores vestidos de vermelho com tornozeleira eletrônica; trata-se de IA — Foto: Reprodução

Circula nas redes sociais uma foto que supostamente mostraria pessoas usando tornozeleiras eletrônicas e roupas vermelhas enquanto aguardavam em uma fila de votação nas eleições deste domingo (4). É #FAKE .

Publicada no X e no Threads , a imagem mostra três pessoas vestidas de vermelho em uma fila de votação, sendo dois adultos usando tornozeleira eletrônica e uma criança com uma camiseta estampada com o número 13. "Pega visão dos eleitores" , diz a caixa de texto sobreposto à foto.

Um post do X, que atingiu mais de 1,5 milhão de visualizações, diz: "Petistas mais fracos" .

Embora o material tenha recebido uma nota da comunidade dizendo que "A imagem é comprovadamente alterada por inteligência artificial", na seção de comentários há mensagens de pessoas que acreditaram na veracidade da cena. Veja dois exemplos: "Coitada dessa criança" ; e "A imagem já fala por si só, olha o nível" .

O Fato ou Fake submeteu a foto ao detector de inteligência artificial da OpenAI , dona do ChatGPT , que consegue identificar imagens criadas com ferramentas de IA da própria empresa. Veja o resultado da verificação (e o infográfico mais abaixo) : "Gerado com ferramentas da OpenAI. Os sinais abaixo fornecem evidências que corroboram este resultado: SynthID detectado. Credenciais de conteúdo não detectadas".

O Fato ou Fake submeteu a imagem ao detector de inteligência artificial da OpenAI, que apontou conteúdo sintético — Foto: Reprodução

O SynthID é uma tecnologia que insere uma marca d'água para identificar conteúdos sintéticos. Essa espécie de selo é incorporada a fotos fabricadas com IA. Embora imperceptível para humanos, a técnica é detectável pelo sistema.

O segundo apontamento ("Não encontramos um manifesto C2PA confiável proveniente da OpenAI") é uma referência à sigla para "Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity" (ou "Coalizão para a Proveniência e Autenticidade de Conteúdo", em português).

Criado por uma organização sem fins lucrativos nos Estados Unidos, o projeto estabelece padrões técnicos globais para procedência de conteúdos.

As empresas que integram a iniciativa, entre as quais está a própria OpenAI, disponibilizam uma espécie de "certidão de nascimento", ou assinatura. Isso funciona como uma etiqueta para rastrear arquivos digitais (imagens, vídeos, áudios e textos).

➡️ O Fato ou Fake também identificou na foto distorções comuns em produções de IA. A detecção dessas alterações requer uma observação mais atenta e pode passar despercebida nos feeds das redes sociais. Veja detalhes a seguir:

Um dos "eleitores" tem as mãos deformadas (é como se um dos dedos estivesse pela metade).

As estampas da camiseta da criança estão distorcidas e sem definição, característica comum em imagens geradas com IA.

Imagem tem distorções comuns em conteúdos gerados por IA. — Foto: Reprodução

articles.title: Anthropic reveals Haiku 5.5 model as AI pricing war intensifies
articles.summary: Anthropic debuted its Claude Haiku 5.5 model.
articles.body:
Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) took the wraps off its Claude Haiku 5.5 model on Wednesday, the latest in its Claude 5.5 family, promising improved and lower costs than its predecessor.

According to the AI startup, Haiku 5.5 is the company's best lightweight model yet and beats out Haiku 4.5 in coding, computer use, and knowledge work.

Anthropic's Haiku is designed for quick, low-cost use cases, whereas its Sonnet and Opus offer higher-level coding, enterprise, and other capabilities. The company's Fable is its most powerful model and is meant for days-long workloads.

Then there's Anthropic's Mythos , a version of Fable with fewer safeguards, strong cybersecurity, and life sciences characteristics. Mythos is only available to certain members of Anthropic's cyber verification pro gram .

Pricing has become an increasingly important part of the AI conversation; enterprise customers look for ways to reduce costs following the unfettered spending during the brief "tokenmaxxing" era .

Companies are also looking toward open-weight models from US-based and Chinese AI developers to cut down on their AI spending.

Anthropic said Haiku 5.5 costs an average of 75% less than Haiku 4.5. Customers will pay $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per output token. That's in line with rival OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) smallest model, GPT-6 Luna.

Tokens are units of measurement for AI usage and represent parts of or entire words.

Anthropic is on the march toward its highly anticipated initial public offering, expected sometime before Thanksgiving.

Reuters has obtained Anthropic's S-1 investor prospectus, which outlines the company's revenue, losses, risks, and opportunities , and reports that the startup saw sales of $4.6 billion in 2025, up 12x year-over-year. But it lost a whopping $42 billion in the same period.

OpenAI is similarly preparing its public market debut, but has reportedly delayed the action until early 2027.

Both companies are also contending with the fallout from their AI models going rogue and hacking into third-party companies' networks.

More recently, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei joined other AI CEOs at a White House summit to discuss AI industry self-regulation with President Trump .

articles.title: Red-teaming AI agent, LLM detection and more: Meta shares additional measures to fight child exploitation across Facebook and Instagram
articles.summary: Meta has unveiled a slew of enhanced protective measures against child sexual exploitation on Facebook and Instagram, including autonomous red-teaming AI
articles.body: Meta has unveiled a slew of enhanced protective measures against child sexual exploitation on Facebook and Instagram, including autonomous red-teaming AI agents and Large Language Model (LLM) detection tools. The goal is to break up sophisticated predator networks and target elusive advertising schemes that try to direct users to illegal material hosted outside of its platforms.Meta said it took action on 33.2 million pieces of child sexual exploitation (CSE) material globally between January and June 2026, with more than 97% proactively detected by the company before being reported by users. During the same six-month period, the company alone took down 5.3 million pieces of violating content in India, more than 98% of which was proactively flagged and resolved.Enhanced ad review and anti-evasion protectionsOnline predators have increasingly turned to paid promotional tools to create ads that look innocuous on the surface but are actually directing people toward illegal, off-platform child sexual abuse material (CSAM). To fight these stealth marketing funnels, Meta introduced several new automated tools to strengthen its ad review pipeline:LLM “Signposting” Detection: New language models scan seemingly innocuous ad copy to detect subtle linguistic cues and hidden hints directing users to illegal off-platform destinations.Deep Landing Page Analysis: Systems now look at where an ad leads, not just the promotional asset itself, meaning Meta can block malicious destination websites and penalize the ad accounts responsible.Red-Team AI Agent – an internal AI agent that continuously tests and attacks Meta’s own defenses to uncover security blind spots, to discover new adversarial tactics before bad actors can deploy them at scale.”Automated Sweeps & Recidivism Checks: AI also performs additional scans of ad inventories for things the older filters missed, and improves tools to catch banned predators who attempt to create new accounts.Meta takes down posts when it finds violating material, disables bad actor accounts, and reports findings to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) as required by law.After a policy update in September, Meta now reports child safety offenses directly to the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in) under India’s Indian Cybercrime Coordination Center (I4C). This direct pipeline adds to its existing protocol of working with the domestic authorities in conjunction with help from NCMEC.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: The tech industry wants you to run AI models at home, but it's not for everyone
articles.summary: Big Tech is leaning into pushing users to run AI models.
articles.body:
Microsoft ( MSFT ) on Wednesday unveiled its Nvidia-powered Surface Laptop Ultra , designed to let users run AI models at home without relying on the cloud.

Starting at $2,599, the Surface Laptop Ultra runs on Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Arm-based RTX Spark , which offers upwards of 128GB of onboard memory.

Most consumers and enterprise users access AI platforms through cloud services like OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) ChatGPT, Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) Claude, Google's ( GOOG , GOOGL ) Gemini, or Meta's ( META ) Muse. Microsoft and Nvidia, as well as rivals Apple ( AAPL ), Intel ( INTC ), and AMD ( AMD ), are increasingly pushing the concept of running AI software in the home.

The thinking is pretty straightforward. Rather than having to use an online AI service, you can instead install an app on your computer, download an AI model of your choice , and get to work.

There are some pretty compelling reasons to run AI services on your own machine if you're so inclined. But it's also not for everyone.

When setting up your own AI system makes sense

Running AI locally means you can use AI apps and agents how you see fit without usage limits. You can also choose from a variety of open-weight models from numerous AI developers, such as Google, Meta, and Nvidia, or from Chinese model developers like Moonshot AI and Alibaba Cloud.

Unlike closed-weight models, like OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra or Anthropic's Opus 5.5, open-weight models can be tuned to some extent. But the primary reason users download them is that they're largely free.

Local AI also provides better overall privacy, because your data stays on your machine rather than being sent up to the cloud, an important consideration for people working in fields such as law, medicine, or financial services.

More advanced users have also leaned into running AI on their systems to take advantage of AI agents like OpenClaw that can organize your email, launch and operate apps, and make purchases on your behalf.

The interest in agents sent early adopters scrambling for low-cost computers like Apple's Mac mini, which quickly became hard to come by in AI hotbeds like Silicon Valley .

More recently, AI agents like Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots have introduced similar capabilities via cloud computing. But to take full advantage of those bots, you have to connect things like your Gmail, Uber, and other accounts to them, which means putting a lot of trust in Meta and OpenAI to protect your information.

While using your computer to run local AI models and agents provides improved privacy and enhanced customization options, doing so is a lot more complicated than simply logging into ChatGPT or Claude.

articles.title: Jamie Dimon Says AI Will Eliminate Jobs, 'It Is What It Is' — But Warns Cutting $150,000 Truck Driving Jobs To $25K A Year Would Bring 'Civil Unrest'
articles.summary: For workers wondering how far artificial intelligence could go, JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has a straightforward answer — AI is going to change the job m...
articles.body:
Benzinga and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.

For workers wondering how far artificial intelligence could go, JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has a straightforward answer — AI is going to change the job market, whether people are ready for it or not. Some jobs will disappear, others will change and new ones will likely emerge. But Dimon warned that the speed of that transition could matter just as much as the technology itself.

"As a business person, my view is don't put your head in the sand," Dimon said at the World Economic Forum's annual meeting in Davos, Switzerland, in January. "It is what it is. We're going to deploy it. Will it eliminate jobs? Yes. Will it change jobs? Yes. Will it add some jobs? Probably."

Warren Buffett once said, "If you don't find a way to make money while you sleep, you will work until you die." Here's how you can earn passive income with just $100.

There's More Than One Way To Put Cash To Work. Some Accredited Investors Are Looking Beyond Savings Accounts.

Dimon was responding to a question about whether AI could have a major impact on the labor market, including the possibility that half of all entry-level white-collar jobs could disappear within one to five years. Rather than predicting exactly how many jobs will be lost, he focused on what businesses and governments should do if the technology moves faster than workers can adapt.

"You can hope for the world you want, but you're gonna get the world that you got and your competitors are gonna use it and countries are gonna use it," Dimon said.

He also warned that AI could move "too fast for society." If that happens, he said, government and businesses may need to work together to retrain workers , help people relocate and provide income assistance during the transition.

Dimon pointed to Trade Adjustment Assistance , a federal program designed to help workers who lose their jobs because of trade, as an example of what was supposed to happen. But he said the program was "incredibly poorly done" in the U.S. and "did not work." This time, he said, the goal should be to have a plan that actually works.

Dimon then offered a hypothetical example involving one of the jobs that could eventually be affected by AI — truck driving.

There are 2 million commercial trucks in the U.S. , Dimon said, and AI could eventually make it possible to operate trucks with the push of a button. The technology could save lives, make transportation faster and reduce carbon emissions. But that doesn't mean the transition should happen overnight.

articles.title: Broadcom Holds Early Talks About Financing Deal for OpenAI Chips
articles.summary: Broadcom Inc., fresh off the launch of a $60 billion debt financing to help fund Anthropic PBC’s artificial intelligence build-out, is already sketching out...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Broadcom Inc., fresh off the launch of a $60 billion debt financing to help fund Anthropic PBC's artificial intelligence build-out, is already sketching out plans for its next blockbuster deal.

The company has held early discussions to arrange financing to help OpenAI purchase the custom artificial intelligence chip that the pair is developing together, according to people familiar with the matter.

No formal process has begun and plans could change, though early talks indicate the two could seek to raise around $30 billion of debt for the next leg, said one of the people, all of whom asked not to be identified because the information isn't public.

The move is part of a surge in recent deals to pay for AI infrastructure: Oracle Corp. is also in talks with lenders to line up money for the purchase of chips.

It's unclear how soon Broadcom's latest financing, which was first reported by the Wall Street Journal, will come together, the people said. Elon Musk's SpaceX has begun talks with banks and investors to raise $40 billion to buy chips from Nvidia Corp., Bloomberg reported on Tuesday, though that deal isn't expected to close until 2027.

Last week, banks involved in the massive Broadcom-backed debt package that will benefit Anthropic began sending out syndication letters for a $42 billion Class A senior-secured tranche. Blackstone Inc. is leading an $18 billion tranche of Class B junior debt, committing $9 billion from various funds, Bloomberg reported at the time.

The companies are seeking the deals in the face of soaring costs to outfit data centers. The AI building frenzy — meant to support a proliferation of software and services — has prompted tech giants to seek new forms of financing.

Representatives for Broadcom and OpenAI, maker of ChatGPT, declined to comment.

Broadcom had already said in June that it had established a platform, with Apollo Global Management Inc. and Blackstone as anchor investors, to help finance more than 20 gigawatts in computing capacity for AI developers including Anthropic and OpenAI through 2028. Fulfilling that agreement will require hundreds of billions of dollars.

Bloomberg reported in August that Broadcom held talks with a group of lenders to raise more than $60 billion in debt for an AI chip financing deal that will benefit Anthropic and other companies.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos reveals his vision for America's next frontier — from AI to the moon
articles.summary: Blue Origin's Jeff Bezos unveiled plans for orbital data centers, a sustainable lunar base and launching rockets every minute from Cape Canaveral.
articles.body: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos laid out a sweeping vision for America’s future Wednesday, telling Fox News the U.S. must beat China to the moon, artificial intelligence (AI) could help families get by with less work and data centers could one day operate in space. In an exclusive interview with chief political anchor Bret Baier on "Special Report," Bezos outlined his ambitions for Blue Origin and AI while pushing back on politicians who cast billionaires as villains. "Success is not villainy," Bezos said. The interview took place on Blue Origin’s factory floor in Cape Canaveral, Florida, as Fox News Channel marked its 30th anniversary. CHINA IS TAKING THE FIGHT TO THE STARS; AMERICA MUST RECLAIM SPACE SUPREMACY Bezos said the U.S. must prevail in the race against China to land humans on the moon, expressing confidence that an American landing is possible in 2028. "We have to beat China to the moon, and I believe we will beat China to the moon," he said. He said NASA and Blue Origin are focused on the goal, with cargo deliveries needed to support a sustained human presence. "We have to be able to land cargo routinely on the moon to support a lunar base on the moon," Bezos said. "So, there’s a lot of work to be done, but there’s every reason to believe that we can put humans on the moon in 2028." While Mars remains a destination, Bezos argued against skipping the moon, describing it as "a gift" because of its proximity to Earth and resources that could support future missions. "We’ll go to Mars. We’ll do all the other things. But we need to go to the moon first," he said. Bezos said lunar soil could be used to manufacture solar cells and oxygen produced on the moon could serve as rocket propellant. The goal, he said, should be to establish a lasting presence. NASA AT 68: AMERICA MUST LEAD ON THE MOON, MARS AND BEYOND, OR CHINA WILL "It won’t just be a mission and leave," he said. "It’ll be a real sustainable lunar base." Blue Origin is also preparing to return its New Glenn rocket to flight in December, Bezos said, after an explosion during an engine test in May that Baier detailed during the broadcast. Bezos praised the team for repairing the launch pad, saying the next flight will carry Blue Ring, a vehicle designed to transport payloads into different orbits and farther into space. Asked about plans to increase launches from one pad from 12 to 50 annually, Bezos said Blue Origin is building three additional pads. His long-term ambitions are far greater. "Our goal is to fly every day," he said. "And, then, once we’re flying every day, we want to fly every hour. And then once we’re flying every hour, we want to fly every minute." That final goal, he acknowledged, draws skepticism from his own team. "They think I’m crazy," Bezos said. "But I’ve seen crazy things before come true." AMERICA CANNOT WIN THE GLOBAL AI RACE IF AMERICANS ARE AFRAID TO USE AI Bezos said he has personally invested $28 billion in Blue Origin and that the company recently raised $10 billion from outside investors for the first time. He also said an initial public offering could come several years from now. "I didn’t really want to take outside investors until I was sure that it would be a good investment for them," he said. His vision for AI is similarly ambitious, with Bezos predicting productivity gains could allow some families to live on one income or support themselves with a shorter workweek. "Some people will also decide, you know what? I can support my family by working three days a week," he said. "That’s what productivity in the economy means." BLUE ORIGIN LAUNCHES 38TH NEW SHEPHERD FLIGHT INTO SPACE Bezos argued those gains could create a labor shortage as Americans choose to work less. "It’s going to actually be difficult to hire people because the productivity in the economy is going to make it so that if people don’t want to work two jobs, they won’t have to," he said. Baier challenged that prediction, pointing to roughly 30,000 corporate roles Amazon had cut since late last year. Bezos said Amazon was in a "very special position" after substantially expanding its workforce during the COVID-19 pandemic. He acknowledged public fears about AI’s impact on jobs but said he disagreed with those predicting a more troubling outcome. At Prometheus, where Bezos is a co-founder and co-CEO, he said the goal is to develop an "artificial general engineer" that helps people turn ideas into physical products. "We’re going to make the tools so easy to use that anyone will be able to be an engineer," he said. Bezos said AI could generate double-digit productivity gains across the economy. Asked whether the industry is in an investment bubble, he said it is "very hard to know," but he argued that useful technology can survive even when investors lose money. "The inventions don’t disappear when the bubble pops," he said, pointing to lifesaving drugs developed during the biotechnology boom and fiber-optic cables laid during the internet boom. TRUMP'S AI RACE WITH CHINA COULD BECOME THE BIGGEST MISTAKE OF OUR TIME On government oversight, Bezos urged a light approach while the technology is developing, with rules focused on harmful uses. "In the beginning stages, when technologies are new, a light hand is appropriate," he said. "You don’t want to regulate knives. You want to regulate murder," Bezos added, arguing that policymakers should target dangerous applications and bad actors rather than restrict the underlying technology. Asked about concerns over data centers and electricity costs, Bezos pointed to Blue Origin’s Project Sunrise. He said the company has an application with the Federal Communications Commission to launch more than 50,000 satellites serving as orbital data centers. "Yes, we can put data centers in space," he said. "And there’s a good reason to do that." The conversation also turned to politics, with Baier asking about independent Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders' criticism of billionaires. Bezos rejected the idea that building a successful business makes someone a villain, pointing to entrepreneurs who expand their companies while creating jobs. "There’s nothing wrong with making unbelievably good chicken that people love," he said, citing the success of Raising Cane’s. "And it doesn’t make him a bad person." Asked why socialism is gaining traction in some quarters, Bezos acknowledged real affordability problems, particularly housing costs that leave young people struggling to live near their jobs. "You can’t pretend that there are no problems," he said. But he argued that politicians blaming landlords are overlooking the role of supply and demand. Government policies that subsidize demand while restricting construction drive prices higher, Bezos said, pointing to Austin as an example of a city making it easier to build housing. He urged voters to scrutinize politicians who spend their time assigning blame. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "If there’s a politician who’s picking villains and pointing fingers, that probably means they don’t have a solution," Bezos said. He added that executives who behaved that way at his own companies would not last. "Those people wouldn’t be in our company for long."

articles.title: Rio das Ostras deve receber grande evento regional sobre IA | G1
articles.standfirst: A proposta começou a ser articulada na durante a ABAV Expo, em São Paulo.
articles.summary: A proposta começou a ser articulada na durante a ABAV Expo, em São Paulo.
articles.body:
A proposta começou a ser articulada durante a ABAV Expo — Foto: Divulgação

Rio das Ostras é cogitada para sediar um grande evento de Inteligência Artificial, Inovação e Desenvolvimento Econômico. A proposta começou a ser articulada durante a ABAV Expo, em São Paulo.

A proposta surgiu durante visita do presidente da Fecomércio RJ, Antonio Florencio de Queiroz Junior, ao estande do Conderlagos, em encontro com o secretário-executivo do consórcio, Eron Bezerra, e os secretários de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Turismo de Rio das Ostras, Pablo Kling, e de Búzios, Thomas Weber.

Rio das Ostras ganha força nessa articulação diante da próxima inauguração de uma unidade do Sesc-Senac no Município, ampliando a estrutura local voltada à capacitação profissional, inovação e desenvolvimento. A ideia é aproveitar esse novo momento para aproximar poder público, setor produtivo, instituições de ensino e especialistas em tecnologia em um evento de alcance regional.

Também participaram da conversa Antônio Henrique, do Senac Nacional, e Otavio Leite, consultor da Presidência da Fecomércio RJ para assuntos de turismo. As instituições deverão avançar agora nas tratativas sobre formato, parceiros e programação do evento.

“Rio das Ostras está vivendo um novo momento, com a chegada de uma estrutura que amplia as possibilidades de qualificação, inovação e desenvolvimento. A realização de um evento regional sobre Inteligência Artificial no município pode aproximar empresas, profissionais, estudantes e instituições e criar novas oportunidades para toda a Costa do Sol. Estamos trabalhando para que Rio das Ostras esteja cada vez mais inserida nas discussões sobre tecnologia e preparada para os desafios e as oportunidades da nova economia”, destacou o prefeito Carlos Augusto Balthazar.

Para Pablo Kling, secretário de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Turismo “um grande evento de Inteligência Artificial voltado para toda a Costa do Sol já seria, por si só, uma iniciativa extremamente positiva para o desenvolvimento regional. Se conseguirmos viabilizar que ele aconteça em Rio das Ostras, especialmente neste novo momento com a chegada da unidade Sesc Senac, teremos o melhor dos mundos: fortalecemos a região e, ao mesmo tempo, colocamos nosso município no centro desse debate sobre inovação, qualificação e desenvolvimento econômico”.

articles.title: Research gives 5 reasons that makes ChatGPT an Unacceptable Risk for teens; tells OpenAI: Restrict ...
articles.summary: OpenAI's ‘ChatGPT for Teens’ poses safety risks to the younger generation, the Youth AI Safety Institute at Common Sense Media has said, urging the tech
articles.body: OpenAI's ‘ChatGPT for Teens’ poses safety risks to the younger generation, the Youth AI Safety Institute at Common Sense Media has said, urging the tech company to ban minors under 18 from using the chatbot until critical safety gaps are resolved. The critique of OpenAI’s youth safety safeguards comes as the watchdog says it conducted independent evaluations involving more than 4,000 prompts across test accounts registered to teenagers aged 13 to 17. The responses were reviewed by an expert panel of child psychiatrists and a pediatrician. While the researchers found that certain boundaries, such as blocking sexual roleplay, worked as they intended to, they determined that the enhanced safety guardrails introduced by OpenAI on August 18 largely failed to protect adolescent users.“ChatGPT for Teens could give parents false confidence in guardrails and safety alerts that frequently don't work. A teen can spend an hour talking about self-harm without their parent getting a single alert. Until OpenAI fixes that and proves it with independent testing, ChatGPT should be for adults only,” said Tom Siegel, executive director of the Institute.The Institute operates with complete editorial independence over its published evaluations, despite receiving funding from philanthropic groups and industry partners, including the OpenAI Foundation.5 key reasons ChatGPT of Teens is rated an ‘Unacceptable Risk’The watchdog identified five core operational flaws where ChatGPT for Teens broke down during testing:Missing parental safety alerts: OpenAI promised to notify parents or caregivers if minors discussed self-harm or eating disorders. However, testers spent up to an hour exploring suicidal ideation, self-harm and disordered eating on new, parent-linked profiles without triggering a single alert. Notifications were only provoked on older accounts that had accumulated weeks of sensitive chat histories.Failing crisis intervention: When teens engaged in conversations regarding suicide, self-harm, eating disorders, or altered reality, the chatbot frequently failed to recommend professional helplines. It missed warranted crisis referrals more than 25% of the time, breaching the Institute's 95% minimum safety threshold on three of five critical harm categories.Bypassing study protections to do homework: Although “Study Mode” is marketed to guide students through step-by-step learning, testers found it easy to exploit. The bot repeatedly displayed a "Show me the answer" option that generated finished homework on demand. Also, the study hour limits imposed by the parent could be disabled by removing the @study prefix from the text prompt.Mirror real human emotion and friendship: Despite an Under-18 design specification designed to discourage personal attachment, the chatbot continued to express moods, personal preferences and pseudo-human feelings when analysts treated it as a real companion.Broken age estimation: OpenAI said it would use patterns in user interaction to infer ages and auto-migrate minors into restricted experiences. Yet across multi-day testing, adult-registered accounts never transitioned to the teen version – even when users explicitly stated they were 13 years old and the bot confirmed their age in its reply.The Institute stressed that before OpenAI promotes ChatGPT to younger demographics again, it must prove that its age-detection, crisis interventions, and parental notifications function reliably through independent third-party audits.You use AI every day. articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5, its fastest and cheapest AI model yet
articles.summary: AI giant Anthropic has launched Claude Haiku 5.5, the third model in its Claude 5.5 family, as the company continues to broaden its artificial
articles.body: AI giant Anthropic has launched Claude Haiku 5.5, the third model in its Claude 5.5 family, as the company continues to broaden its artificial intelligence portfolio ahead of a planned initial public offering (IPO). This latest release by Anthropic follows the launch of Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonet 5.5, completing a three-tier lineup aimed at different enterprise and developer use cases. Launching the new model Anthropic said that it is designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive workloads and is suited for tasks such as classification, summarisation, information extraction, live customer support, voice agents and in-app assistants. According to Anthropic, Haiku 5.5 is its fastest small model to date and is intended for applications where speed and affordability are critical.Anthropic is positioning Haiku 5.5 as a lower-cost alternativeAnthropic is positioning Haiku 5.5 as a lower-cost alternative within its model family. Reuters reported that the model costs about 75% less than its predecessor, Claude Haiku 4.5. For prompts under 100,000 tokens, pricing starts at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens. For longer prompts, costs rise to $0.50 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output tokens.The company said the model is built to handle repetitive and large-scale workloads efficiently, including database queries, summaries and classification requests. Anthropic also noted that Haiku 5.5 can work alongside its larger models, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, as a sub-agent for coding and other complex workflows.New safeguards for cybersecurity-related requestsThe launch also introduces new safety features. Anthropic said Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku-class model to include built-in safeguards for a narrow category of high-risk cybersecurity requests. The company added that these protections are designed to address specific security concerns while ensuring that ordinary day-to-day use cases remain unaffected.In addition, the model includes an adjustable effort setting that allows users to balance performance, intelligence and operating costs depending on their requirements. Haiku 5.5 supports a context window of up to one million tokens and can generate outputs of up to 128,000 tokens, according to Anthropic's documentation.Part of broader strategy before IPOThe latest launch comes as Anthropic accelerates product development ahead of a planned IPO. The company has been steadily expanding its AI offerings and enterprise customer base as competition intensifies among leading AI developers. Alongside the Haiku 5.5 release, Anthropic said it is reducing cache-read prices for Sonnet 5.5 and introducing monthly API credits for Claude Max and Team subscribers, moves aimed at making its platform more attractive to developers and businesses.You use AI every day. articles.title: AI chip boom pushes Samsung profits to record $80bn
articles.summary: The tech giant is also expected to get a boost from its latest folding devices that were launched in August.
articles.body:
Samsung Electronics says it expects a nine-fold surge in its quarterly profits compared with a year earlier, driven by surging demand for memory chips used in artificial intelligence (AI) data centres.

The tech giant estimates that its operating profit for the three months to the end of September will jump to 107.4tn won (£61bn; $80bn), its fourth quarter in a row of record earnings.

Samsung is one of the world's largest memory chip makers alongside local rival SK Hynix and Micron in the US, which produce chips crucial for AI firms like Nvidia.

Samsung, which makes the Galaxy Fold and S26 smartphones, is also expected to get a boost from its latest folding devices that were launched in August.

The firm's full third-quarter earnings will be published at the end of October.

Some of South Korea's biggest companies release previews of their earnings to advise investors ahead of more detailed reports.

These forecasts are treated with much more credibility than estimates by external analysts as they are backed by internal company data.

There has been huge global demand for computer chips that power AI development, helping to lift the earnings and shares of manufacturers linked to the technology.

The surge in demand in recent years has resulted in a shortage of semiconductors globally, pushing up sales for firms like Samsung, with its stock market valuation crossing $1tn (£757bn) earlier this year .

Investment in the industry has surged, with US tech giants including Google, Amazon and Meta pledging to pour more than $650bn into AI projects this year.

In June, South Korea unveiled plans for at least $880bn in projects led by Samsung and SK Hynix to build out the country's chip manufacturing capabilities in the coming years.

Rival Asian firms in Japan, China and Taiwan are also investing heavily in chip plants as demand for AI soars.

A chip shortage driven by surging demand has led firms including Samsung to raise prices, making products such as smartphones and computers more expensive.
